analysis:
Reviewed all 15 units. No security regression was identified.

1) EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift head 37-42 adds the exact ID "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged list. It is an exact-match string with no prefix or case folding, so other IDs stay contiguous, and explicit config and the kill switch (lines 69-77) still override it. Automatic paged failures may degrade (lines 103-107), which is the existing behavior. The test at head line 52-54 asserts the resident prefix RAM cache stays off, so the T-041 posture is unchanged. Paged attention plus the wider automatic concurrency (test head 260-270) affect availability and capacity only. No change was made to cacheSalt, the SSD tier, or attestation.

2) FlintNativeProtocolConstraint.swift head 152-162 adds maskCacheKey, which returns the interned state id. It returns nil when the constraint is exhausted, the budget is 0 or the state is unknown. The same lines set allowsChainedDecode=true. FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift head 72-91 maps matched nodes to key -1. Scanning nodes reuse the base key, which must be >=0, so the keys cannot collide. Both nextState paths (head 164-185 and 93-109) are unchanged, so exhaustion still fails closed with a nil transition.

These are output-shaping and integrity concerns (T-007-adjacent), not confidentiality concerns. Constraint masks derive from request tools and stops, not from prompt plaintext.

Open question for integration: the CBv2 sampler that consumes maskCacheKey and allowsChainedDecode is not supplied. The keys are only meaningful per constraint instance. Integration should verify that device-mask caches are scoped per request/constraint and are dropped on completion. Integration should also verify that speculative chained decode never emits or commits a token that confirmed nextState rejects. A cross-request key collision would let one request's tool/stop mask constrain another request, which is an integrity issue (T-007).

The test files change only test coverage.
